clue.text: Bank worker's more comfortable getting article for uniform

indicators.note: getting introduces what comes into the word in place of something else
for marks a swap: one letter put in place of the other

parts.note: cushier means softer, more comfortable
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A bank clerk finds a cosier life by trading their uniform for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting ... for' puts A where the U of CUSHIER stood.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller who handles cash at a bank counter is a bank employee.

clue.text: Caught old man getting fat

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
old man is slang for husband, a hubby

explanation.surface: Someone's husband is caught putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby means plump or fat.

clue.text: Learn about end of Oliver Hardy

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to study is to learn

indicators.note: end of says take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to read up on how Oliver Hardy's career ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like part of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy and hardy both mean robust and strong.

clue.text: Drunk, I turned all grumpy

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that drink made them bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone surly and bad-tempered is grumpy.

clue.text: In theatre curtains come round at intervals

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the words theatre curtains

explanation.surface: Stage curtains periodically sweep around in a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again repeatedly.

clue.text: Brown top from Tesco with peculiar fit

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: Someone throws a strange fit over a brown top bought at a supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesco is a British supermarket chain; 'peculiar' looks like part of the definition but supplies RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an outburst of temper, a kind of fit.

clue.text: Timid camper's covering topless resident

parts.note: a tent covers a camper

indicators.note: topless says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a native is a resident of a place

explanation.surface: A shy camper's tent covers a resident without a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentative means hesitant, uncertain, timid.

clue.text: Cracked almonds?

definitions.meaning: almonds are an example of hard-shelled fruit, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Almonds with their shells broken open.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both crazy and edible kernels such as almonds.

clue.text: Swine blocking the way?

parts.note: pigs on the highway, read as rude drivers who hog the road

explanation.surface: Pigs standing in the road and stopping traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names inconsiderate drivers who obstruct others; swine as an insult.

clue.text: Scatter seed in my imagination

indicators.note: scatter means throw about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Picturing oneself scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the inner faculty of seeing things mentally.

clue.text: Typical American university student is after top grade

indicators.note: the student's letter is placed after the grade letter

parts.note: A is the top grade in exams
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: A typical American college student is chasing the best marks.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual and typical both describe what normally happens.

clue.text: Hold back prisoner with small drill

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
to drill someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Guards restrain an inmate during a short exercise session.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to restrict or keep in check.

clue.text: Frightful shock lasting 24 hours?

parts.note: a shock of hair that looks frightful, for the whole of one day

explanation.surface: A terrible fright that keeps you rattled for an entire day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as a fright, but it is a shock of hair; a frightful mop that stays that way for a day.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a day when one's hair looks awful and everything goes wrong.

clue.text: Some flipping criticism — hopefully they show resistance

indicators.note: flipping says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone hopes that a bit of harsh criticism will toughen people up.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical resistance is measured in units named after Georg Ohm.

clue.text: Various bananas sir mislaid

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A knight has lost track of assorted bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Various things are unlike one another, different.

clue.text: Amazingly doctor slips, hurrying out of hospital

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
out of says a letter leaves the pool

parts.note: H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: A medic stumbles while rushing out of the hospital, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a person but is the anagram signal; 'out of' removes H from SLIPSHURRYING before mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs describe something happening in an astonishing, unexpected way.

clue.text: Small Parisian coat contains old cake

parts.note: petit is French for small

indicators.note: contains says one piece holds the other

parts.note: fur is an animal's coat

explanation.surface: A little Parisian's coat has an old cake in the pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A petit four is a small fancy cake served after a meal.

clue.text: Being hostile to work and assuming an attitude

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
posing is adopting a pose, an attitude

explanation.surface: Antagonistic at work, and striking a pose about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing means resisting or being against something.

clue.text: First person to call upper-class European something sweet

parts.note: me is the first-person pronoun
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: I'll be the first to phone a posh European with sweet nothings.
explanation.definitionFit: A meringue is a sweet dessert of baked whipped egg white.

clue.text: This sentence is in this page by Sterne, awfully edgy

indicators.note: awfully suggests the name is badly jumbled

parts.note: edgy means nervous, tense

explanation.surface: A self-referential remark about a nervous page written by Laurence Sterne.
explanation.walkthrough: Sterne is the 18th-century novelist of Tristram Shandy; 'awfully' rearranges STERNE into RESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's own verb 'is' is in the grammatical form for now, not past or future.

clue.text: Upset faces after he loses husband's respect

indicators.note: after places the overturned word behind the shortened word
loses says a letter is taken away from the word
Upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: to face is to meet, so faces is meets

explanation.surface: A disgruntled man loses his spouse's regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses MEETS; 'loses' takes H from HE to leave E.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard, respect.

clue.text: Lock up trainee

definitions.meaning: to lock up means to confine, as in wartime
a trainee doctor or junior worker on placement

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to confine, and the noun means a junior trainee.

clue.text: Poet's ordinary recording

parts.note: vid is short for video, a recording

explanation.surface: A poet makes an everyday recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman writer of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: One working with rock star initially moans dreadfully following sound quality

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the sound-quality word
initially says take just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: tone is the quality of a sound

indicators.note: dreadfully says the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rock star complains bitterly about the quality of the sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock star' looks like a musician; 'rock' belongs to the definition. 'dreadfully' turns MOANS into MASON.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason cuts and lays stone, so works with rock all day.

clue.text: Horrid adult breaking new pen

indicators.note: breaking says the letter breaks into the other pieces

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A horrible grown-up snaps a brand new pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means unpleasant, horrid.

clue.text: Regularly consult king

indicators.note: Regularly says take every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Advice to seek a monarch's counsel often.
explanation.definitionFit: Cnut was an 11th-century king of England, Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: Clever, fashionable chap cut debts

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: cut says the word is trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a chap
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A smart, trendy fellow reduces what he owes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious means inventive and clever.

clue.text: Lord, for example, imprisoned in story

indicators.note: imprisoned in says one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: a story can mean a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A tale in which a lord is locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord to whom service is owed.

clue.text: Larger kitchen tool in Spain? On the contrary

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside another
On the contrary flips the stated containment: the tool holds Spain, not the other way

parts.note: a grater is a kitchen tool for shredding cheese
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bigger kitchen gadget is found in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the tool goes in Spain; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so E goes inside GRATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater and larger are synonyms for bigger in size.

clue.text: Cart pulled back miles by an outdoor labourer

indicators.note: pulled back says the word is read backwards

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: A worker outdoors drags a cart back some miles.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardman works in a yard, such as a railway or farm yard.
